theory: Prompts are packaged, strictly rendered instruction assets whose exact source participates in experimental identity, while user slash templates expand into recorded user input. Template source, rendered claim-specific text, and backend response contracts are related but distinct identities.
instead_of: Treat prompts as incidental string literals or let a malformed user template change built-in command behavior; that would hide instruction changes and make failures dependent on call-site formatting.

absorption.rationale: Adding staged templates and user commands fits the loader, but obtaining an exact backend-specific prompt identity requires the separately acknowledged hash/manifest change.

world_mapping.rationale: Source loading, strict rendering, staged/batch payload identities, and user-command expansion map to the different ways instructions reach a model.

abstraction.rationale: A resource loader and one Jinja environment support installed package assets, while template expansion exposes a deliberately smaller user-facing language.

justification.rationale: The code explains why hashes cover raw template source, why unrelated interactive prompts stay out of staged identity, and why cached installed resources are assumed stable.

honest_limits.rationale: The Codex structure-instruction hash asymmetry is explicitly recorded; user templates reject missing arguments, reserved names, links, and unreadable input instead of silently fabricating instructions.

rehearsals.requirement: Add another required field to a prompt template.
rehearsals.why: StrictUndefined makes missing renderer input an explicit PromptError at the shared renderer.

rehearsals.requirement: Add a project-specific slash command with positional arguments.
rehearsals.why: The user template loader and placeholder expander already model that operation without modifying built-ins.

rehearsals.requirement: Record a prompt hash matching exactly the structure instructions sent by each backend.
rehearsals.why: The source explicitly states the Codex/backend asymmetry and the need for a per-backend identity plus manifest schema change.
